article_content: A NATO airstrike in eastern Afghanistan has killed a leader of the Pakistani Taliban. The international alliance says the operation on Friday in the Shigal district in Kunar province killed Maulawi Zakaria and several others. Media reports indicate that 15 insurgents were killed in the attack. NATO says Zakaria, also known as Jamal, was responsible for planning attacks against civilians and coordinating the movement of fighters and weapons, as well as attacks against Afghan and coalition forces. Zakaria reportedly replaced Maulvi Faqir Mohammed last year as the leader of the Taliban in Pakistan's Bajaur tribal agency, near the border with Afghanistan. Some information for this report was provided by AP, AFP, and Reuters.
